correctness.rationale: For fixed finite n with epsilon=1/n and the depth-limit epsilon=0, the exact local expansion at u=1 is -z+(epsilon-2)z²+(epsilon²/3-2epsilon+8/3)z³+O(z⁴), so the second iterate is z-kappa z³+O(z⁴) with kappa=(4/3)(2-epsilon)(5-2epsilon)>0. The two-step contraction and reciprocal-square telescoping yield k(u_k-1)²→kappa^-1 in the original single-step clock. For the infinite-depth f(u)=u exp(2u(1-u)), every orbit enters a compact invariant interval, and a hypothetical prime 2-cycle u<1<v would require s=u+v in (1,2), delta=v-u, delta²=s(2-s), and log(v/u)=(s-1)delta; the strict logarithmic-mean inequality instead gives log(v/u)>2delta/s>(s-1)delta. Coppel's no-2-cycle interval theorem then gives convergence; positive trajectories cannot tend to the repelling boundary zero. Thus all positive initial states converge to one; nonfinite-hits have k^-1/2 coefficient sqrt(3/40). This makes no global finite-depth claim.
